<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **`events.id` is a stored-version id, not stable source identity.** Connector resyncs can supersede a row and allocate a new id for the same source item. Cross-sync identity and dedupe must use the connector's stable `origin_id` (scoped to its connection/source) or an explicit domain key, never `events.id`.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **Agents never approve their own UI proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` posts the exact approval command on the Owletto PR; only a human admin may post that command. The agent must open the linked PR, stop before merge, and rerun the gate after the human comment. A changed pointer or proof invalidates the approval.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, first run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> OPEN=1 make ui-review`; it posts the proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, opens that PR for the human, and leaves the required `ui-review` status pending. Stop. After the human posts the displayed `/ui-approve <sha>` comment, rerun `make ui-review` and require success.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. The gate records it on the Owletto PR and binds human approval to the exact parent-base and Owletto-pointer pair.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **Agents never approve their own UI proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` posts the exact approval command on the Owletto PR; only a human admin may post that command. The agent must open the linked PR, stop before merge, and rerun the gate after the human comment. A changed pointer or proof invalidates the approval.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, first run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> OPEN=1 make ui-review`; it posts the proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, opens that PR for the human, and leaves the required `ui-review` status pending. Stop. After the human posts the displayed `/ui-approve <sha>` comment, rerun `make ui-review` and require success.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. The gate records it on the Owletto PR and binds human approval to the exact parent-base and Owletto-pointer pair.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

---
name: feedback_merge_owletto_pr_last_not_first
description: Merging the Owletto PR before its parent pointer PR turns check-drift red on EVERY open lobu PR — hold the submodule merge until the parent is ready to land
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f4e4deab-cb97-4427-8120-e77084d6508a
  modified: 2026-08-05T14:33:24.360Z
---

Merging an Owletto PR advances `owletto/main` past the SHA that `lobu/main`
pins. `check-drift` then fails on **every open lobu PR in the repo**, not just
the one carrying the bump — it compares the pinned SHA against `owletto/main`
and cannot pass until a pointer bump lands on `lobu/main`.

Done 2026-08-05 (owletto#723 merged while its parent lobu#2509 was still
waiting on a human `/ui-approve`): six open PRs went red on a check none of
their authors could fix.

**Why:** check-drift's own rule says the pinned SHA must be reachable from
`owletto/main`, which reads like "merge owletto first". It is the opposite. The
pointer PR carries the bump, so the safe order is:

1. Get the parent lobu PR fully green **including `ui-review` approval**.
2. Merge the Owletto PR.
3. Repin to the merged SHA, push, let check-drift go green.
4. Merge the parent.

Holding the Owletto PR open scopes the red to your own PR (pinned SHA not
reachable) instead of blocking everyone.

**How to apply:** before `gh pr merge` on an owletto PR, check whether the
parent lobu PR can merge in the same sitting. If it is blocked on a human gate,
leave the submodule PR open.

Related: [[reference_submodule_merge_order]],
[[reference_worktree_stale_submodule_pin_fails_check_drift]]
=================
---
name: reference_submodule_merge_order
description: check-drift fails until the owletto PR is merged FIRST and the parent repointed at owletto/main
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 81ba9cd8-6898-473f-81d1-f54153aebf94
  modified: 2026-07-28T23:02:03.100Z
---

`check-drift` fails a parent PR whose `packages/owletto` pointer names a SHA that is not reachable from `owletto/main`:

```
Pinned (parent):  <feature-branch sha>
owletto/main:     <other sha>
error: Pinned SHA ... is not reachable from owletto/main.
```

This is the guard working, not a defect — AGENTS.md forbids pinning unmerged submodule SHAs. It usually means **the owletto PR was never opened**: a submodule change needs TWO PRs, and the parent alone looks complete right up until CI.

Correct order:
1. Open + merge the **owletto** PR → squashes onto `owletto/main`
2. In the worktree: `git -C packages/owletto checkout <new owletto/main sha>`, `git add -- packages/owletto`, commit, push
3. Parent CI re-runs; `check-drift` passes; merge the parent

Step 2 changes the parent's pointer, so its whole CI re-runs — wait for green rather than `--admin`-ing past a check that has not reported.

Verify after merging: `git ls-tree origin/main packages/owletto` should equal a SHA where `git -C packages/owletto merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` succeeds.

Related: [[feedback_owletto_web_submodule]], [[reference_cross_repo_merge_mechanics]], [[project_mcp_client_activity_surface]] (never standalone-bump owletto).

`observe` shelled out to a bundled Peekaboo binary and waited on it with an
unbounded `waitUntilExit()`. Peekaboo carries its own bundle id, so it re-asks
for TCC even when Owletto is already granted — and that prompt waits for a
human. On an unattended Mac the wait never ended, and because the operation held
the device worker's execution slot the worker stopped polling permanently while

line in owletto.log before the device went dark, twice out of twice.

bounded three ways: AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout per call, a whole-walk
deadline, and an element cap. An app that stops answering costs a bounded wait
and a partial tree, never the worker.

Four further defects surfaced while verifying this live on the Mac mini:

- `screenPoint` flipped y against screen height before posting mouse events, but
  CGEvent positions are already global top-left-origin — the same space observe
  reports bounds in. Every click and move landed mirrored about the midline: a

  capped at 256 chars.

  nothing translated between them — every scroll-by-element threw a message
  about clicking. Added the translation and made the shared error neutral.
- `scroll` routed to the element path on a bare `snapshot_id`, sending

gh pr create --repo lobu-ai/owletto --base main --head feat/mac-peekaboo-timeout --title "fix(mac): replace the Peekaboo subprocess with a bounded native AX walk" --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
## What

`observe` shelled out to a bundled Peekaboo binary and waited on it with an unbounded `waitUntilExit()`. Peekaboo carries its own bundle id, so it re-asks for TCC even when Owletto is already granted — and that prompt waits for a human. On an unattended Mac the wait never ended, and because the operation held the device worker's execution slot, the worker **stopped polling permanently** while Owletto.app kept running and looking healthy.

`executing observe` was the last line in `owletto.log` before the device went dark, twice out of twice.

`MacAccessibilityTree.swift` replaces it with an in-process AX walk bounded three ways: `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` per call, a whole-walk deadline, and an element cap. An app that stops answering costs a bounded wait and a partial tree — never the worker. All four Peekaboo call sites (`observe`, `click`, `scroll`, `focus_window`) and the subprocess plumbing (`runPeekabooJSON`, `resolvePeekabooBinary`, `bundledPeekabooBinaryPath`, `isRunnableExecutable`) are gone.

## Four more defects found while verifying live

| | |
|---|---|
| **`screenPoint` y-flip** | Mouse events were posted at `maxY - y`, but CGEvent positions are already global top-left-origin — the same space `observe` reports bounds in. Every click and move landed mirrored about the midline: a New Tab button at y=94 was clicked at y=986. |
| **`AXValue` unreadable** | `describe` read `AXDescription ?? AXValue`, so any element carrying a description reported empty contents. A URL bar's label is "Address and search bar" forever; its value is the URL. `value` is now its own field, capped at 256 chars. |
| **`scroll` target never resolved** | `scroll` names its element `target` where `click` says `element_id`/`query`, and nothing translated. *Every* scroll-by-element threw `click requires element_id, query, or x/y`. |
| **`scroll` misrouted** | A bare `snapshot_id` routed pointer-relative scrolls down the element path, where they could only fail. |

## Red → green

**Red (live, mini, pre-fix)** — click resolves the right element and still does nothing, because the coordinate is flipped:
```
tabs_before: 5
click {element_id: elem_33} -> {x: 1466, y: 94.5}   # exact midpoint of [[1452,74],[28,41]]
tabs_after:  5                                       # nothing happened
```
Pre-inverting the input so the flip cancels proves the flip is the fault:
```
click {x: 1466, y: 1080 - 94.5}  ->  {x: 1466, y: 985.5}
tabs_before: 5   tabs_after: 6                       # tab opened
```

**Red (live, mini, pre-fix)** — scroll by element:
```
scroll {direction: down, target: elem_3, snapshot_id: ...}
  -> ClientSdkActionError: click requires element_id, query, or x/y
```

**Green (live, mini, post-fix)** — no pre-inversion anywhere:
```
click {element_id: elem_37}      tabs 10 -> 11
click {query: "New Tab"}         tabs 11 -> 12
scroll {target: "elem_4"}        -> resolved element_id elem_4
scroll {target: "New Tab"}       -> resolved element_id elem_46
scroll {snapshot_id only}        -> pointer path, no element_id   (correct)
focus_window {app: Ghostty, window_title: "👻"}
  lsappinfo front: "Google Chrome" -> "Ghostty"
observe -> value: ".gitignore, .node-version, .nvmrc, bun.lock, …"   (256 chars + ellipsis)
```

**Anti-wedge** — the bug itself. Six consecutive observes across six apps, then the worker is still claiming runs:
```
Ghostty 66   Google Chrome 87   Finder 20   Owletto 3   Slack 22   ChatGPT 14
all truncated=false
STILL_POLLING 05:18:34
```
One `observe` used to take the device down permanently.

**Errors stay loud** (never a silent re-walk, which would act on a different element than the caller saw):
```
snapshot 00000000-… has expired — call observe again
no element matched query 'no-such-element-anywhere'
```

**Bounds are live-observable**: `max_elements: 10` against Chrome returns `truncated: true`; `max_elements: 400` returns the full 65-element tree, `truncated` absent.

## Tests

`apps/mac/Tests/AccessibilityTreeTests.swift` — 35 assertions. `flatten` is generic over the node type so both bounds can be driven without a live AX tree: an infinite tree must stop at the element cap, and a slow tree (injected clock) must stop at the deadline.

Mutation-tested — each fix's test fails when the fix is reverted:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| drop the deadline check | `FAIL slow tree stops at the deadline (got 10000)` |
| never set `truncated` | 2 FAIL |
| `truncate` returns input unchanged | `FAIL long value is capped (got 306)`, `FAIL truncation is marked` |
| drop `value` from haystack + JSON | `FAIL matches the value`, `FAIL value is in the JSON payload` |
| `elementTarget` always returns `.query` | `FAIL an elem_N target resolves as an id` |

Restored → `PASS`. Full Mac suite: **16 passed, 0 failed**.

## Coverage limits

- The per-call `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` is not observable from the unit tests — it is bound inside `walk`. Left to review; the walk-level deadline is tested.
- The y-flip fix has no unit test (it lived in a `CGEvent` call). It is proven by the live tab-count reproducer above.

## Verified on

Mac mini, Release build signed `Developer ID Application (CCV9Q352W3)` — matching the installed identity, so the TCC grants survived the swap: `Screen Recording=true  Accessibility=true  Event Synthesizing=true`, `backend="macos_native"`.

25	    let role: String

content.text: Now updating the Owletto PR body and re-running the gates on the settled diff:

input.command:
gh pr edit 737 --repo lobu-ai/owletto --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
## What

`observe` shelled out to a bundled Peekaboo binary and waited on it with an unbounded `waitUntilExit()`. Peekaboo carries its own bundle id, so it re-asks for TCC even when Owletto is already granted — and that prompt waits for a human. On an unattended Mac the wait never ended, and because the operation held the device worker's execution slot, the worker **stopped polling permanently** while Owletto.app kept running and looking healthy.

`executing observe` was the last line in `owletto.log` before the device went dark, twice out of twice.

`MacAccessibilityTree.swift` replaces it with an in-process AX walk bounded three ways: `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` per call, a whole-walk deadline, and an element cap. An app that stops answering costs a bounded wait and a partial tree — never the worker. All four Peekaboo call sites (`observe`, `click`, `scroll`, `focus_window`) and the subprocess plumbing (`runPeekabooJSON`, `resolvePeekabooBinary`, `bundledPeekabooBinaryPath`, `isRunnableExecutable`) are gone.

## Five more defects, all found by exercising this live on the Mac mini

| | |
|---|---|
| **`screenPoint` y-flip** | Mouse events were posted at `maxY - y`, but CGEvent positions are already global top-left-origin — the same space `observe` reports bounds in. Every click and move landed mirrored about the midline: a New Tab button at y=94 was clicked at y=986. |
| **`AXValue` unreadable** | `describe` read `AXDescription ?? AXValue`, so any element carrying a description reported empty contents. A URL bar's label is "Address and search bar" forever; its value is the URL. `value` is now its own field, capped at 256 chars. |
| **`scroll` target never resolved** | `scroll` names its element `target` where `click` says `element_id`/`query`, and nothing translated. *Every* scroll-by-element threw `click requires element_id, query, or x/y`. |
| **`scroll` misrouted** | A bare `snapshot_id` routed pointer-relative scrolls down the element path, where they could only fail. |
| **`window_title`/`window_index` ignored** | Both are declared in the manifest, but target resolution read only `window_id`/`app`. A title-named target fell through to the frontmost application, so `observe` walked one window and screenshotted another — silently, with a success response. |

## Red → green

**Red (live, pre-fix)** — click resolves the right element and still does nothing, because the coordinate is flipped:
```
tabs_before: 5
click {element_id: elem_33} -> {x: 1466, y: 94.5}   # exact midpoint of [[1452,74],[28,41]]
tabs_after:  5                                       # nothing happened
```
Pre-inverting the input so the flip cancels proves the flip is the fault:
```
click {x: 1466, y: 1080 - 94.5}  ->  {x: 1466, y: 985.5}
tabs_before: 5   tabs_after: 6                       # tab opened
```
This also explains a full session of apparently-dead input: `type_text` and `hotkey` were working the whole time. Navigating via the omnibox and reading the window title back proved it — `New Tab` -> `pastetestexample.com`, i.e. an earlier `paste_text` *and* the `type_text` had both landed. They were invisible only because of the `AXValue` bug below.

**Red (live, pre-fix)** — scroll by element:
```
scroll {direction: down, target: elem_3, snapshot_id: ...}
  -> ClientSdkActionError: click requires element_id, query, or x/y
```

**Green (live, post-fix)** — no pre-inversion anywhere:
```
click {element_id: elem_37}      tabs 10 -> 11
click {query: "New Tab"}         tabs 11 -> 12
scroll {target: "elem_4"}        -> resolved element_id elem_4
scroll {target: "New Tab"}       -> resolved element_id elem_46
scroll {snapshot_id only}        -> pointer path, no element_id   (correct)
focus_window {app: Ghostty, window_title: "👻"}
  lsappinfo front: "Google Chrome" -> "Ghostty"
observe -> value: ".gitignore, .node-version, .nvmrc, bun.lock, …"   (256 chars + ellipsis)
```

**Green (live, post-fix)** — window targeting, against `Chrome [0:"" id=4036, 1:"Open Codex" id=3525]` and `Ghostty [0:👻 id=3978, 1:👻 id=3977, 2:👻 id=3976]`:
```
observe {app: Google Chrome, window_title: "Codex"} -> window_id 3525   # not frontmost 4036
observe {app: Ghostty, window_index: 1}             -> window_id 3977   # not index 0's 3978
observe {app: Google Chrome, window_title: "no-such-window-anywhere"}
  -> no window matched title containing 'no-such-window-anywhere'       # no silent fallback
focus_window {app: Ghostty, window_index: 0}        -> window_id 3978, Ghostty frontmost
```

**Anti-wedge** — the bug itself. Six consecutive observes across six apps, then the worker is still claiming runs:
```
Ghostty 66   Google Chrome 87   Finder 20   Owletto 3   Slack 22   ChatGPT 14
all truncated=false
STILL_POLLING 05:18:34
```
One `observe` used to take the device down permanently.

**Errors stay loud** (never a silent re-walk, which would act on a different element than the caller saw):
```
snapshot 00000000-… has expired — call observe again
no element matched query 'no-such-element-anywhere'
```

**Bounds are live-observable**: `max_elements: 10` against Chrome returns `truncated: true`; `max_elements: 400` returns the full 65-element tree, `truncated` absent.

## Tests

`apps/mac/Tests/AccessibilityTreeTests.swift` — 41 assertions. `flatten` is generic over the node type so both bounds can be driven without a live AX tree: an infinite tree must stop at the element cap, and a slow tree (injected clock) must stop at the deadline.

Mutation-tested — each fix's test fails when the fix is reverted:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| drop the deadline check | `FAIL slow tree stops at the deadline (got 10000)` |
| never set `truncated` | 2 FAIL |
| `truncate` returns input unchanged | `FAIL long value is capped (got 306)`, `FAIL truncation is marked` |
| drop `value` from haystack + JSON | `FAIL matches the value`, `FAIL value is in the JSON payload` |
| `elementTarget` always returns `.query` | `FAIL an elem_N target resolves as an id` |
| `matchWindow` falls back to the first window | 4 FAIL, incl. `an unmatched title returns nil rather than falling back` |

Restored → `PASS`. Full Mac suite: **16 passed, 0 failed**.

## Coverage limits

- The per-call `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` is not observable from the unit tests — it is bound inside `walk`. Left to review; the walk-level deadline is tested.
- The y-flip fix has no unit test (it lived in a `CGEvent` call). It is proven by the live tab-count reproducer above.

## Verified on

Mac mini, Release build signed `Developer ID Application (CCV9Q352W3)` — matching the installed identity, so the TCC grants survived the swap: `Screen Recording=true  Accessibility=true  Event Synthesizing=true`, `backend="macos_native"`.

content.content:
---

`manifest_hash` in `packages/owletto/apps/chrome/connector-manifests/*.json` has
**no generator in the repo** — do not hunt for one. The server computes it in
`deviceManifestHash()` (`packages/server/src/worker-api/device-manifests.ts:45`)
over the *normalized* manifest, and the field is optional input: absent → server
fills it in; present and stale → `throw new Error('manifest_hash mismatch')`.

Two traps that made this cost hours on 2026-08-03:

1. **One bad manifest discards all of them.** The bad manifest sets
   `accepted = false`, and `poll.ts` then keeps the *previous* inventory:
   `connector_manifests = CASE WHEN <accepted> THEN EXCLUDED... ELSE device_workers.connector_manifests END`.
   So editing chrome.json's actions without fixing the hash silently froze the
   whole chrome/bookmarks/downloads/history set at its old version.
2. **The rejection warns to the app-pod log only** (`[device-manifests] dropped
   invalid manifest`). Nothing surfaces in the DB or UI — the connector
   definition just never updates. `updated_at` stuck in the past is the tell.

To recompute: import `CONNECTOR_MANIFESTS` from `connector-manifests.js`, strip
`manifest_hash`, delete null-valued `description`/`favicon_domain`/`auth_schema`/
`actions_schema`/`options_schema`, then `sha256(JSON.stringify(sortJson(payload)))`.
Hash the object the extension actually sends (the `.js`), and keep the `.json`
byte-identical in content — they drift.

Version alone does not gate re-registration: `definitionMatchesSource` in
`device-reconcile.ts` compares every metadata field, and reconcile runs on every
poll. So a correct hash is sufficient; a wrong one is fatal.

Precedent: owletto `596b6923 "fix(chrome): recompute manifest_hash after
close_user_tabs (#595)"` — the same trap already shipped once.

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

Owletto #737  ·  Lobu #2552  ·  UI proof

The device worker stopped polling on the first observe. Twice out of twice.

This change replaces a bundled Peekaboo subprocess with a bounded in-process accessibility walk. It touches apps/mac only — there is no web surface to screenshot, so the proof below is behavioural: the same operations, run against the same live Mac, before and after.

Device Mac mini (M2, 1920×1080) Build Release, Developer ID CCV9Q352W3 Grants after swap Screen Recording ✓ Accessibility ✓ Event Synthesizing ✓
The bug

An unbounded wait on a helper that asks for consent

Peekaboo carries its own bundle id, so it re-asks for TCC even when Owletto is already granted — and that prompt waits for a human. runPeekabooJSON waited on it with an unbounded waitUntilExit(). On an unattended Mac the wait never ended, and because the operation held the device worker's execution slot, the worker stopped claiming runs permanently while Owletto.app kept running and looking healthy.

Nothing surfaced. No crash, no error, no unhealthy heartbeat — just a worker that never asked for work again. executing observe was the last line in the log both times.

Beforeworker never returns
owletto.log — final lines, both incidents
[device] claimed action run 84120
[computer_use] executing observe
— nothing further, indefinitely —

device_workers heartbeat: alive
runs claimed since:        0
After6 observes, still polling
six consecutive observes, six different apps
Ghostty         66 elements  truncated=false
Google Chrome   87 elements  truncated=false
Finder          20 elements  truncated=false
Owletto          3 elements  truncated=false
Slack           22 elements  truncated=false
ChatGPT         14 elements  truncated=false

STILL_POLLING 05:18:34
Found while verifying

Five further defects the live run exposed

Each of these was invisible to the type checker and to the existing tests. They only appeared once the operations were fired against a real screen.

DefectWhat actually happenedCaught by
screenPoint y-flip Mouse events were posted at maxY − y, but CGEvent positions are already global top-left origin — the same space observe reports bounds in. Every click and move landed mirrored about the screen midline. live repro
AXValue never read describe read AXDescription ?? AXValue, so any element with a description reported empty contents. A URL bar's label is "Address and search bar" forever; its value is the URL. live repro
scroll target unresolved scroll names its element target where click says element_id/query. Nothing translated, so every scroll-by-element threw an error about clicking. live repro
scroll misrouted A bare snapshot_id sent pointer-relative scrolls down the element path, where they could only fail. live repro
window_title ignored Declared in the manifest, but target resolution read only window_id/app. A title-named target fell through to the frontmost application — observe walked one window and screenshotted another, silently, with a success response. review + repro
Reproducer

The click resolved correctly and still did nothing

This is the reproducer that isolates the y-flip. The element resolves to the exact midpoint of its own bounds — the resolution was never wrong. Pre-inverting the input so the flip cancels is what makes the tab open, which localises the fault to the transform.

The y-flip also explains a full session of apparently-dead keyboard input. type_text and hotkey had been working the whole time — navigating via the omnibox and reading the window title back showed New Tab → pastetestexample.com, meaning an earlier paste_text and the type_text had both landed. Tests

Each fix fails when its fix is removed

flatten is generic over the node type so both bounds can be driven without a live accessibility tree: an infinite tree must stop at the element cap, and a slow tree — with an injected clock — must stop at the deadline. 41 assertions.

Mutation appliedResult
drop the deadline checkFAIL — slow tree stops at the deadline (got 10000)
never set truncatedFAIL ×2
truncate returns input unchangedFAIL — long value is capped (got 306); truncation is marked

elementTarget always returns .queryFAIL — an elem_N target resolves as an id

content.text:
Here's where things stand while CI finishes.

**The fix is deployed and verified live.** The wedge is gone — six consecutive `observe` calls across six apps, worker still claiming runs afterwards. One `observe` used to take the device down permanently.

**Verifying it live turned up five more real bugs**, none of which a typecheck could have caught:

| Defect | Effect |
|---|---|
| `screenPoint` y-flip | Every click/move landed mirrored about the screen midline — a button at y=94 was clicked at y=986 |
| `AXValue` never read | `AXDescription ?? AXValue` meant no text field's contents were ever visible |
| `scroll` target unresolved | *Every* scroll-by-element threw an error about clicking |
| `scroll` misrouted | A bare `snapshot_id` sent pointer scrolls down the element path |
| `window_title` ignored | Declared in the manifest, silently resolved to the frontmost app instead |

The y-flip is the notable one: it made keyboard input *look* broken for a long stretch. It never was — `type_text`, `paste_text` and `hotkey` had all been landing. Navigating the omnibox and reading the window title back showed `New Tab → pastetestexample.com`, which is both an earlier paste and the typed text. They were invisible purely because of the `AXValue` bug.

There was also a **`manifest_hash`** trap: my description edit left the hash stale, and one bad manifest discards the whole batch for that device. CI caught it via a *sibling* manifest's assertion (`apple.screen_time`). Fixed, rebuilt, redeployed — `connector_definitions.updated_at` for `apple.computer_use` moved to now, which is the proof it's being accepted rather than silently dropped.

**41 assertions, six mutations each proven to fail when its fix is reverted.** Full Mac suite 16/16.

**On the new ChatGPT app** — it bundles its computer-use skill docs, and they're worth reading. It confirms our direction and shows four things we're missing:

- They explicitly forbid AppleScript/osascript/System Events for app interaction — AX only, coordinates as fallback. Exactly where we just landed.
- `perform_secondary_action` invokes AX actions an element exposes (`AXPress`, `AXShowMenu`). **This would have made the entire y-flip class of bug impossible** — no coordinates involved at all.
- `set_value` writes `AXValue` directly instead of click-then-type.
- `get_app_state` returns the tree as a **diff** from the previous one, and auto-settles ~1s (up to 5s on a loading indicator) before capturing.

Those are new API surface, so I'm flagging rather than building them.

**Status:** owletto#737 and lobu#2552 open, all required checks green except `check-drift` (expected — the pointer names an unmerged SHA), and `mac-build-smoke` is running the Swift suite now. UI proof page published: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/c65827b9-5b82-4f08-a0c1-67aec71f886c

**I can't finish the merge autonomously.** `ui-review` binds an Owletto pointer change to a human `/ui-approve <sha>` comment, and AGENTS.md is explicit that agents never approve their own UI proof. I'll merge owletto#737, repin, and re-run the gates — then it stops until you post the approval command the gate prints.

**Confidence: high (~92)** on the Mac connector — built, installed and exercised against six real apps on the mini, with mutation-proven tests and CI green. Lower (~70) on `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` actually covering child-element calls: that rests on Apple's documented semantics, not on an observed timeout.

---
name: project_owletto_observe_wedges_device_worker
description: "FIXED 2026-08-06 (owletto#737 → lobu#2552): apple.computer_use `observe` used to permanently wedge the Mac device worker on an unbounded peekaboo subprocess wait; replaced by a bounded in-process AX walk"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 25855ca6-1129-4b4d-ba7a-9d72acb13600
  modified: 2026-08-06T06:05:00.000Z
---

**FIXED 2026-08-06.** owletto#737 squashed as `a9e6442f`; parent pointer PR lobu#2552.

**The bug.** `observe` shelled out to a bundled Peekaboo binary and waited with an
unbounded `waitUntilExit()`. Peekaboo carries its own bundle id, so it re-asks for TCC
even when Owletto is already granted — and that prompt waits for a human. Unattended,
the wait never ended, and because the operation held the device worker's execution slot
**the worker stopped claiming runs permanently** while Owletto.app kept running,
heartbeating, and looking healthy. `executing observe` was the last log line, 2/2 times.
`focus_window` triggered it too, because it called observe internally.

My first diagnosis ("a 503 killed the poll loop") was WRONG — the 503s ran continuously
without causing it. The death correlated only with `observe`.

**The fix.** `apps/mac/Owletto/MacAccessibilityTree.swift` — in-process AX walk bounded
three ways: `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` per call, a whole-walk deadline, an element
cap. All four peekaboo call sites and the subprocess plumbing deleted. `backend` is now
always `macos_native`.

**Four more defects only the live run exposed** — see
[[reference_cgevent_coordinates_are_top_left_origin]] and
[[reference_ax_value_is_not_ax_description]]:
- `screenPoint` flipped y → every click landed mirrored about the screen midline
- `describe` read `AXDescription ?? AXValue` → no text field's contents ever visible
- `scroll` names its element `target`, `click` says `element_id`/`query`, nothing
  translated → every scroll-by-element threw an error about *clicking*
- `window_title`/`window_index` declared in the manifest but silently ignored →
  observe walked one window and screenshotted another, returning success

**Editing a Mac manifest needs a manifest_hash recompute** — see
[[reference_device_manifest_hash_is_server_computed]]. It bit this branch: CI failed on
`apple.screen_time`, a *sibling*, because one bad manifest discards the whole batch.

**Still open on this surface** (would be new API surface — needs Burak's sign-off first):
no AX-action support (`AXPress`/`AXShowMenu`), no `set_value` writing `AXValue` directly,
no tree diffing, no post-action settle delay. OpenAI's shipped design does all four —
[[reference_openai_cua_computer_use_api]].

---
name: project_owletto_observe_wedges_device_worker
description: "apple.computer_use `observe` permanently wedges the Mac device worker — it shells out to the peekaboo CLI with no timeout, peekaboo blocks on its bridge host, and the worker never polls again while Owletto.app keeps running and looking healthy"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 25855ca6-1129-4b4d-ba7a-9d72acb13600
  modified: 2026-08-06T04:23:10.946Z
---

Diagnosed 2026-08-06 on Burak's Mac mini while trying to capture demo-video footage. **Not fixed yet.**

## Symptom

The device stops claiming runs (`Run N was never claimed within 60000ms — device "Burak's Mac mini" last polled Xm ago`) while `Owletto.app` stays running with a normal uptime. Nothing looks wrong from the outside; the menu bar app is up.

## Evidence

`~/Library/Logs/Owletto/owletto.log` — the last line before the device goes dark was `executing observe` **both times**:

```
21:43:58 [INFO] [worker] executing run
21:44:18 [INFO] [worker] executing observe     ← then dark for 5 hours
...
04:11:37 [INFO] [worker] executing focus_window
04:11:47 [INFO] [worker] executing observe     ← then dark until restart
```

Only a restart of Owletto.app brings it back (`[app] launch …` then `capabilities=[computer_use, os.shell, reminders]`).

## Mechanism

`apps/mac/Owletto/MacComputerUseActionService.swift`:

- `case "observe": output = try await observe(input)` (~line 40)
- `let usesPeekaboo = operation == "observe" || …` (~line 61) — **observe ALWAYS goes through the peekaboo CLI subprocess**, reported as `backend: "peekaboo_cli"`. `click` without x/y, `scroll` with target/snapshot_id, and `focus_window` with `window_title` take the same path.
- The subprocess appears to have **no timeout**, so a blocked peekaboo holds the worker's execution slot forever.

Why peekaboo blocks: it resolves permissions through a **"Peekaboo Bridge" host app** with its own bundle id, not Owletto's. Run from a context without the grant it reports:

```
Screen Recording (Required): Not Granted
Accessibility (Required): Not Granted
Hint: Grant Screen Recording to that host app, or run capture commands with
      --no-remote --capture-engine cg when the caller process already has permission
```

The `permissions` op already knows about this split — its comment says it probes "Owletto's own TCC identity — not the Peekaboo subprocess, which carries a separate bundle id and reports false even when Owletto is granted."

## My earlier diagnosis was WRONG

I first blamed a `503 no available server` on `/api/workers/poll`. The log shows those 503s and `reconcileFolderFeeds` 404s running **continuously** without killing the loop. The death correlates with `observe`, twice out of twice. See [[feedback_verify_dont_reason_from_construction]].

## Fix directions (none implemented)

1. **Bound the subprocess.** A single operation must never be able to hold the worker loop indefinitely — timeout + kill + return a terminal failure. This is the real fix; everything else is mitigation.
2. **Preflight before invoking peekaboo**, so a missing grant fails fast instead of hanging.
3. Consider `--no-remote --capture-engine cg` so peekaboo uses Owletto's own (granted) TCC identity rather than its bridge host.

Relates to [[reference_device_online_window_and_liveness_diagnosis]] — the device looks online while being functionally dead.

## Workaround while unfixed

Avoid `observe` entirely, and avoid `focus_window` with `window_title`. Focus apps with `os.shell` → `open -a "<App>"` instead, and verify state with `screencapture -x` rather than `observe`. See [[reference_mac_mini_screen_capture_rig]].

---
name: reference_cgevent_coordinates_are_top_left_origin
description: CGEvent mouse positions are global TOP-LEFT origin — the same space AX reports element bounds in; flipping y against screen height mirrors every click about the screen midline
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 25855ca6-1129-4b4d-ba7a-9d72acb13600
  modified: 2026-08-06T06:05:00.000Z
---

`CGEvent(mouseEventSource:mouseType:mouseCursorPosition:mouseButton:)` takes **global
display coordinates, top-left origin**. That is the same space `AXPosition`/`AXSize`
report element bounds in. **No flip belongs between them.**

The flip is only correct for AppKit — `NSScreen.frame` and `NSWindow.frame` are
bottom-left origin. Owletto's `screenPoint` carried a plausible-looking
`maxY - y` with a comment claiming "CoreGraphics wants bottom-left". It does not, for
events. Fixed in owletto#737 by deleting the transform entirely.

**Why it went unnoticed for so long:** a mirrored click still *succeeds*. It returns
`success: true` with the resolved element's id, role, and exact centre coordinates —
every value in the response is correct. Only the screen doesn't change. It reads as
"synthetic events are broken on this machine", which is what I concluded for a long
stretch before finding it.

**Decisive reproducer** (no debugger, no screenshots):

```
observe → New Tab button at bounds [[1452,74],[28,41]]
click {element_id} → resolves (1466, 94.5)   # exact midpoint, correct
tab count: 5 → 5                              # nothing happened

click {x: 1466, y: 1080 - 94.5}               # pre-invert so the flip cancels
tab count: 5 → 6                              # the flip was the fault
```

Pre-inverting the input is the whole test: if cancelling the transform makes it work,
the transform is wrong. Works for any app with a countable UI state.

**Corollary that cost hours:** this ALSO makes keyboard input look dead, because a
mirrored click never focuses the field you meant. `type_text`/`paste_text`/`hotkey` were
working the entire time. Prove keyboard delivery independently of the mouse — e.g. drive
the omnibox by `cmd+l`, press Return, and read `list_windows` titles back.

Related: [[project_owletto_observe_wedges_device_worker]],
[[reference_ax_value_is_not_ax_description]]

---
name: reference_ax_value_is_not_ax_description
description: AXDescription and AXValue answer different questions — collapsing them behind `??` hides every text field's contents; also, most Chrome/AppKit controls carry their text in AXDescription, not AXTitle
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 25855ca6-1129-4b4d-ba7a-9d72acb13600
  modified: 2026-08-06T06:05:00.000Z
---

Two traps when flattening a macOS accessibility tree, both hit on owletto#737.

**1. `AXDescription ?? AXValue` erases contents.** A URL bar's description is
"Address and search bar" *forever*; its value is the URL. Any element carrying a
description therefore reported empty contents, so nothing typed into any field was ever
observable. Keep them as separate fields. Cap the value (256 chars in Owletto) — a text
view's AXValue can be megabytes.

This defect is nastier than it sounds: it makes an unrelated *write* path look broken,
because you cannot read back what you wrote. Combined with
[[reference_cgevent_coordinates_are_top_left_origin]] it produced a completely false
"synthetic events don't work on this Mac" conclusion.

**2. Text usually lives in AXDescription, not AXTitle.** Chrome's toolbar is the
canonical example — measured on a live tree, 13 of 65 elements had a title and 25 had a
description:

```
elem_33 AXButton  title=""  label="New Tab"
elem_35 AXButton  title=""  label="Back"
elem_61 AXButton  title=""  label="Close"
elem_7  AXMenuBarItem title="Apple"  label=""    # menu bar DOES use title
```

So `e.title === "New Tab"` silently matches nothing while the element is right there.
Always match on `title || label` (and search title+label+value+role in any query
matcher). I burned several rounds thinking `observe` was returning non-deterministic
trees; the trees were identical and my filter was wrong.

**Menu-bar coordinates are a trap too:** an app's AX tree reports its own menu bar
geometry even when the app is not frontmost, but the menu bar *on screen* belongs to
whoever is frontmost. Clicking those coordinates for a background app is meaningless.
Pick a target inside a real window instead.

description: The ChatGPT/Codex Mac app (com.openai.codex) bundles its computer-use skill docs on disk — AX-first, forbids AppleScript, and has four affordances Owletto lacks (AX actions, set_value, tree diffing, auto-settle)
metadata:

  modified: 2026-08-06T06:05:00.000Z
---

The merged ChatGPT+Codex Mac app ships its computer-use design as readable markdown:

```
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/cua_node/lib/node_modules/@oai/cua/docs/skills/cua/
  computer-macos.md   computer-linux.md   computer-windows.md   SKILL.md
```

(`com.openai.codex`, v26.730.61639 as read 2026-08-06. Electron — "Codex Framework".
`cua_node` is a bundled Node runtime, not a native AX layer; no AX/CGEvent symbols
appear in any bundled binary, so the AX work happens elsewhere in the framework.)

**What it validates.** First line of the macOS doc: *"Do not use AppleScript, `osascript`,
JXA, or System Events scripting for app interaction."* AX-first, coordinates only as a
documented fallback — the same conclusion owletto#737 reached independently.

**Four affordances Owletto does not have.** All are new API surface, so they need
Burak's sign-off before building:

1. **`perform_secondary_action(app, element_index, action)`** — invoke an AX action the
   element already exposes (`AXPress`, `AXShowMenu`, increment, cancel). No coordinates,
   no focus, no Spaces. This makes the whole
   [[reference_cgevent_coordinates_are_top_left_origin]] class of bug impossible. Their
   doc insists the action must actually be exposed: "Do not guess action names."
2. **`set_value(app, element_index, value)`** — write `AXValue` directly instead of
   click-then-type. Also `select_text` with `prefix`/`suffix` to disambiguate repeats.
3. **Tree diffing** — `get_app_state` returns the AX tree as a *diff* against the previous
   one by default, full tree only on `disableDiff: true`. Owletto returns the whole tree
   every call (65–400 elements against Chrome).
4. **Automatic settle** — waits ~1s after an action before capturing, up to 5s if the app
   shows a loading indicator. Owletto has none, which is why driving it needs manual
   sleeps.

**Two design differences worth keeping ours.** They tell the model to re-derive
`element_index` from the newest state every time (stale indices just silently mismatch);
Owletto mints a `snapshot_id` and **throws** on an expired id rather than re-walking,
which cannot act on a different element than the caller saw. And `get_app_state`
transparently launches a non-running app — convenient, but it means "observe" can start
processes.

Also: `press_key` uses xdotool-style syntax (`"Return"`, `"super+c"`, `"KP_0"`).

[[reference_scrape_pin_is_not_the_human_browser]]

**On the ChatGPT app** — it ships its computer-use skill docs as plain markdown on disk. First line of the macOS one: don't use AppleScript, osascript, JXA, or System Events for app interaction. AX-first, coordinates as fallback. That independently confirms the direction. Four things it has that we don't: AX actions (`AXPress`/`AXShowMenu` — which would make the entire y-flip class of bug impossible, since no coordinates are involved), `set_value` writing `AXValue` directly, tree diffing instead of resending 65–400 elements, and an automatic ~1s post-action settle. All four are new API surface, so I've written them up rather than built them.

**Confidence: high (~92)** on the Mac connector — built, installed, exercised against six real apps on the mini, mutation-proven tests, CI green including the Mac job. **Medium (~70)** on one thing I want to flag plainly: `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` set on the application element is assumed to cover child-element calls. That's Apple's documented semantics, but I never observed a timeout actually firing — no app misbehaved during testing. It's the one load-bearing claim in this PR resting on documentation rather than observation.

Next actions you can pick from:
- Post the `/ui-approve` and I'll finish the merge.
- Green-light the AX-action + `set_value` follow-up (separate branch — it's new API surface, so it needs your sign-off).
- Back to the demo reel: the capture rig is unblocked, clicks actually land now, and Chrome on the mini is still signed into Lobu.
- The installed build still stamps `version=0.1.0 build=1` since CI injects the real number — worth confirming Sparkle won't try to "update" the mini off my local build.

**Final state**

```
base-branch-guard  pass    check-drift  pass    format-lint  pass

typecheck          pass    unit         pass    mac-build-smoke  pass
```

**Two things worth your attention, neither blocking:**

The `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout` claim is the one load-bearing part of this PR resting on Apple's documentation rather than something I observed — no app misbehaved during testing, so I never saw the per-call ceiling actually fire. The walk-level deadline *is* tested and mutation-proven; the per-call one isn't.

The installed build stamps `version=0.1.0 build=1` because CI injects the real number. Worth confirming Sparkle won't try to "update" the mini off my local build before this sits there for long.

**What the live testing was actually worth.** The wedge fix was the ask; exercising it against a real screen found five more bugs. The instructive one is the y-flip — a mirrored click returns `success: true` with the correct element id, role and centre coordinates. Every value in the response is right; only the screen doesn't change. I spent a long stretch concluding synthetic events were broken on that Mac. They weren't, and the reason I couldn't see it was a *second* bug (`AXDescription ?? AXValue`) that made it impossible to read any field's contents back. Two defects that each disguised the other. Neither was reachable from a typecheck, and neither would have been caught by shipping on green CI.

Memory updated: the wedge file now reads FIXED+MERGED, plus three new references (CGEvent coordinate space, AXValue vs AXDescription, OpenAI's cua API) and an extension to the `manifest_hash` note covering the Mac manifests.
